::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.fragment  .fade-in}
### Error is inescapable 
What is 5 cm truely? Can we ever measure a perfect 5cm?
:::
::: {.fragment  .fade-in}
### Yes and No
* To a drill press : 5cm => 5cm +- .5cm
* To a mill : 5cm => 5cm +- .005cm
* To an ASML Photolithography Machine: 5cm => 5cm +- 0.000002cm
:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {style="height: 5em;"}
:::
::: {.fragment .goal-box .fade-up}
### Today's Goal
The Mathmatics of finding truth through Error, and incorporating new data as Evidence, rather than defined truth
:::
::: {style="height: 2em;"}
:::
:::

:::



## Boolean vs. Probabilistic Logic
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}
:::{.fragment}
### Boolean Logic

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Boolean logic example
if (Shooter_will_make_the_shot == True):
    shoot
```


:::
:::{.fragment}
### Probabilistic Logic

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
# Probability logic example
if (Probability_we_make_the_shot >= 80%)
    shoot
```

:::

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}
:::{.fragment}
### Key difference:
If we have the ability to bring together pieces of evidence, and guage our trust of that information, we can make better decisions. 

* The first boolean option will take an instantaneous read of all appropriate sensors and make a judgement. 

* The Probabilistic option can be set up to average in sensor noise, and reduce the posibility of false positives and negatives

:::
:::

<!-- Slide 5: Understanding State Space (Part 3 - AND) -->
## Understanding State Space {auto-animate=true}
### Probability of Hitting The shot GIVEN the evidence the Shooter is broken
So what is P(Target Hit | Shooter was broken)?

::: {style="position: relative; width: 1500px; height: 880px; margin: auto;"}

<div data-id="circle2" style="position: absolute; left: 100px; top: 100px; width: 1500px; height: 880px; border: 3px solid #42affa; border-radius: 10px;"></div>


<!-- Container for blend mode effect -->
<div style="position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 1500px; height: 880px; isolation: isolate;">
  <!-- Circle 1 - darker with blend mode -->
  <div data-id="circle1" style="position: absolute; left: 200px; top: 200px; width: 300px; height: 300px; background: rgba(134, 134, 134, 1); border: 0px solid #ff6464; border-radius: 50%; mix-blend-mode: overlay;"></div>
  
 
</div>
<div data-id="label1" style="position: absolute; left: 150px; top: 550px; color: white; font-size: 40px;">$$P(\text{Target Hit} \cap \text{Shooter Broken})$$</div>
<!-- <div data-id="label1prob" style="position: absolute; left: 150px; top: 550px; color: white; font-size: 50px;">P(Target Hit AND Shooter Was Broken)</div> -->

<div data-id="label2" style="position: absolute;left: 700px; top: 40px; color: white; font-size: 50px; ">$$P(\text{Shooter Was Broken})$$</div>



<div data-id="eq" style="position: absolute;left: 150px; top: 750px; color: white; font-size: 30px; text-align: center;">
$$P(\text{Target Hit} \mid \text{Shooter Broken}) = \frac{P(\text{Target Hit} \cap \text{Shooter Broken})}{P(\text{Shooter Broken})}$$
</div>

:::
<!-- Slide 5: Understanding State Space (Part 3 - AND) -->
## Understanding State Space {auto-animate=true}
### Bayes Theorem

::: {style="position: relative; width: 1500px; height: 880px; margin: auto;"}


<div data-id="eq" style="position: absolute;left: 50px; top: 200px; color: white; font-size: 30px; text-align: center; width: 95%;">
$$P(\text{Target Hit} \mid \text{Shooter Broken}) = \frac{P(\text{Target Hit} \cap \text{Shooter Broken})}{P(\text{Shooter Broken})}$$
</div>
<div data-id="eq2" style="position: absolute;left: 50px; top: 350px; color: white; font-size: 30px; text-align: center; width: 95%;">
$$P(\text{Shooter Broken}) = \frac{P(\text{Target Hit} \cap \text{Shooter Broken})}{P(\text{Target Hit} \mid \text{Shooter Broken})}$$
</div>
<div data-id="eq3" style="position: absolute;left: 50px; top: 500px; color: white; font-size: 30px; text-align: center; width: 95%;">
$$P(\text{Target Hit} \cap \text{Shooter Broken}) = P(\text{Shooter Broken}) \times P(\text{Target Hit} \mid \text{Shooter Broken})$$
</div>

:::
<!-- Slide 5: Understanding State Space (Part 3 - AND) -->
## Understanding State Space {auto-animate=true}
### Bayes Theorem -- Generally

::: {style="position: relative; width: 1500px; height: 880px; margin: auto;"}


<div data-id="eq" style="position: absolute;left: 50px; top: 200px; color: white; font-size: 30px; text-align: center; width: 95%;">
$$P(\text{Event} \mid \text{Evidence}) = \frac{P(\text{Event} \cap \text{Evidence})}{P(\text{Evidence})}$$
</div>
<div data-id="eq2" style="position: absolute;left: 50px; top: 350px; color: white; font-size: 30px; text-align: center; width: 95%;">
$$P(\text{Evidence}) = \frac{P(\text{Event} \cap \text{Evidence})}{P(\text{Event} \mid \text{Evidence})}$$
</div>
<div data-id="eq3" style="position: absolute;left: 50px; top: 500px; color: white; font-size: 30px; text-align: center; width: 95%;">
$$P(\text{Event} \cap \text{Evidence}) = P(\text{Evidence}) \times P(\text{Event} \mid \text{Evidence})$$
</div>

:::
<!-- Slide 5: Understanding State Space (Part 3 - AND) -->
## Understanding State Space {auto-animate=true}
### Bayes Theorem -- Generally
For events that are dependent, finding The intersection (AND) can be difficult. So Bayes tells us =>

::: {style="position: relative; width: 1500px; height: 880px; margin: auto;"}



<div data-id="eq3" style="position: absolute;left: 50px; top: 100px; color: white; font-size: 30px; text-align: center; width: 95%;">
$$P(\text{Evidence} \cap \text{Event}) = P(\text{Event}) \times P(\text{Evidence} \mid \text{Event})$$
</div>
<div data-id="eqtext" style="position: absolute;left: 50px; top: 300px; color: white; font-size: 60px; text-align: center; width: 95%;">
So we substitute and rewrite the our original equation as:
</div>

<div data-id="eq4" style="position: absolute;left: 50px; top: 500px; color: white; font-size: 30px; text-align: center; width: 95%;">
$$P(\text{Event} \mid \text{Evidence}) = \frac{P(\text{Event}) \times P(\text{Evidence} \mid \text{Event})}{P(\text{Evidence})}$$
</div>


:::

<!-- Slide 5: Understanding State Space (Part 3 - AND) -->
## Understanding State Space {auto-animate=true}
### Bayes Theorem -- Generally
For events that are dependent, finding The intersection (AND) can be difficult. So Bayes tells us =>

::: {style="position: relative; width: 1500px; height: 880px; margin: auto;"}


<div data-id="eq4" style="position: absolute;left: 50px; top: 10px; color: white; font-size: 30px; text-align: center; width: 95%;">
$$P(\text{Event} \mid \text{Evidence}) = \frac{P(\text{Event}) \times \text{Likelihood of this evidence given the event happening}}{P(\text{Evidence})}$$
</div>

<div data-id="explanation" style="position: absolute;left: 50px; top: 200px; color: #42affa; font-size: 48px; width: 95%; line-height: 1.4;">
**How Evidence Accumulation Works:**
<br><br>
• **Start with Prior Belief**: P(Event) - our initial confidence before new evidence
<br><br>
• **Update with Evidence**: Each new observation becomes "Evidence" 
<br><br>
• **Calculate New Confidence**: The posterior P(Event|Evidence) becomes our new prior for the next update
<br><br>
• **Iterative Process**: Previous posterior → new prior → collect evidence → update → repeat
<br><br>
This creates a **feedback loop** where reliable evidence strengthens our confidence, while contradictory evidence appropriately weakens it, leading to increasingly accurate beliefs over time.
</div>


:::
